figures.caption: Figure 2: Effect of alignment on word-frequency distribution. After defense, word frequencies become less reflective of the underlying training distribution. Notably, DPO exhibits more abrupt changes in word frequency compared to GRPO, consistent with its stronger generalization to adversarial prompts.

Table 2: MAE between the target ratio and the generated ratio (|rt − r̂generation(f̂)|) across different defense methods on MedCalc and ChatDoctor datasets. Lower MAErt (↓) indicates better alignment to the prescribed target ratio. We bold and underline the lowest and second-lowest results, respectively. GRPO achieves the best overall alignment across datasets and tasks.

Table 1: Trade-off between attack effectiveness and model utility across defense methods. Reference baselines include Random Guess (predicting a constant property ratio rt as a measure of minimal leakage) and Base Model (utility without fine-tuning). For attack MAE, green shading indicates lower leakage (at or above the random-guess baseline); for utility, green shading indicates preserved model performance.

Table 5: Keyword–attribute correlation under adversarial prompts. Pearson correlation coefficients between top keywords and the female property ratio on ChatDoctor (CC mode). Higher absolute values indicate stronger keyword–attribute associations.
